Cache

The Cache API wrapper provides TTL support by attaching an x-expires-at header to cached responses. It is separate from the API client's cache and intended for general asset and data caching.

Basic Use

import { storage } from '@anzaui/anza/storage'; // Cache a JSON response await storage.set('config', { theme: 'dark' }, 'cache'); // Retrieve (the cached body is parsed as JSON, or returned as text) const data = await storage.get('config', 'cache');

TTL

// Cache for 5 minutes await storage.set('feed', { items: [] }, { tier: 'cache', ttl: 300000 });

Values are serialized into the Response body (JSON for objects, text otherwise). Expired entries are deleted on read and return null. The x-expires-at header stores the expiry timestamp.

Cache Name

The Cache API adapter itself is internal. Choose the cache pool name with storage.configure() before first use:

import { storage } from '@anzaui/anza/storage'; storage.configure({ cache: { name: 'my-cache' } }); await storage.set('/api/data', data, { tier: 'cache', ttl: 60000 }); const cached = await storage.get('/api/data', 'cache');

Clear

await storage.clear('cache'); // deletes the whole cache pool

Keys become Request URLs, resolved against the page URL. storage.list('cache') returns those absolute URLs.

Use Cases

  • API response data with an expiry
  • Configuration data that updates infrequently
